lessons.title: Starter 1 · Statements and questions
lessons.description: Use は and です to make a polite statement, then か to ask a question.

notes.title: Statements with は and です
notes.pattern: 私 は 学生 です
notes.explanation: は marks who or what you are talking about. It is written は but pronounced wa. Put the person’s role next, then です. In this pattern, です makes the statement polite and corresponds to am, is or are.

notes.title: Questions with か
notes.pattern: 友達 は 会社員 です か
notes.explanation: Put か after です to ask a question. あなた means you, but in conversation people often use a name or leave out the person when it is clear who they mean.

cards.english: My friend is a company employee
Is your friend a company employee?

lessons.title: Starter 2 · This and that: これ・それ・あれ
lessons.description: Use これ, それ and あれ to identify something by its distance from you and the listener.

notes.title: Point to something
notes.pattern: これ は 本 です
notes.explanation: Use これ for something near you, それ for something near the listener, and あれ for something away from both of you. Imagine pointing to the object as you speak.

cards.english: That over there is a book
That over there is a chair
That over there is a car
Is that over there a car?
Is that over there a chair?
Is that over there a book?

lessons.title: Starter 3 · Describing with い-adjectives
lessons.description: Describe size and age with 大きい, 小さい, 新しい and 古い.

notes.title: Describe an object
notes.pattern: 本 は 大きい です
notes.explanation: Put an adjective after は to describe something, then finish with です. These adjectives end in い; keep that ending before です.

lessons.title: Starter 4 · Presence and absence: あります・います
lessons.description: Say whether a thing or person is there, and ask about their presence.

notes.title: Say that a thing is there
notes.pattern: 本があります
notes.explanation: が marks the thing whose existence you describe. ある becomes あります in polite speech. Use this verb for things and plants; Japanese often leaves out the location when it is clear.

notes.title: Say that a thing is absent
notes.pattern: 本がありません
notes.explanation: The polite negative of あります is ありません. It means that the thing is not there, or that you do not have it.

notes.title: People and animals: います
notes.pattern: 先生がいます
notes.explanation: For people and animals, use いる, politely います. The person still takes が. A clear location can be left out.

notes.title: Say that a person is absent
notes.pattern: 先生がいません
notes.explanation: The polite negative of います is いません. Keep the distinction: ありません for things, いません for people and animals.

lessons.title: Starter 5 · Possession and “also”: の・も
lessons.description: Link an owner to a thing with の, and add another matching person or thing with も.

notes.title: Whose is it?
notes.pattern: 私の本 / あなたの本
notes.explanation: Put の between the owner and the thing: 私の本 is my book; あなたの本 is your book. Keep this phrase together in the familiar これは…です sentence.

notes.title: Say “also”
notes.pattern: 私も学生です
notes.explanation: Use も when the same description applies to another person. Put it directly after the person you are talking about, in place of は.

notes.title: も after an ownership phrase
notes.pattern: 私の本も新しいです
notes.explanation: Keep the owner and the thing together as one phrase. Put も after that whole phrase when the same description applies to it too.

lessons.title: Starter 6 · Actions and objects
lessons.description: Read, write, and study. Use を with the thing you act on.

notes.title: The object of an action
notes.pattern: 本 を 読みます
notes.explanation: を (pronounced o) marks the object of an action. Put it after the thing being acted on and before the verb.

notes.title: A negative verb ending
notes.pattern: ます → ません
notes.explanation: The ending ません (masen) makes the verb negative. Here, 書きません (kakimasen) means “do not write” or “will not write.”

notes.title: An activity and its verb
notes.pattern: 勉強 します
notes.explanation: 勉強 (benkyō) means “studying.” します (shimasu) means “do.” Together, they describe doing that activity: studying.

notes.title: The same activity with を
notes.pattern: 勉強 を します
notes.explanation: You can also say 勉強をします (benkyō o shimasu). Here, を marks studying as the activity you do. Both forms mean “study.”

lessons.title: Starter 7 · Where and with whom
lessons.description: Locate people and things, say where an action happens, and include a companion.

notes.title: Where someone or something is
notes.pattern: 学校 に 先生 が います
notes.explanation: Start with the place, followed by に (ni), then say who or what is there with が (ga) and います or あります.

notes.title: Where you do something
notes.pattern: 家 で 本 を 読みます
notes.explanation: Use で for the place where you read, write, or study.

notes.title: Doing something with someone
notes.pattern: 友達 と 勉強 します
notes.explanation: と after a person means with that person. Between two nouns, it joins them: 私と友達.

notes.title: Say where someone is
notes.pattern: 先生 と 友達 は 学校 に います
notes.explanation: When you are talking about particular people, put them before は (wa), then give their location with に (ni). This answers “Where are they?” The earlier place-first pattern tells you who is there.

notes.title: Ask for an impression
notes.pattern: 学校 は どう です か
notes.explanation: どうですか asks how something is or what someone thinks of it.

lessons.title: Starter 8 · Now and before
lessons.description: Change familiar statements into negatives and talk about completed actions.

notes.title: Answer yes or no
notes.pattern: いいえ、私 は 先生 ではありません
notes.explanation: はい means yes; いいえ means no. After a noun, use ではありません for am not, is not, or are not. は in this ending is pronounced wa.

notes.title: A role in the past
notes.pattern: 私 は 学生 でした
notes.explanation: Use でした after a noun to describe the past. Its negative is ではありませんでした.

notes.title: A completed action
notes.pattern: 本 を 読みました
notes.explanation: Change ます to ました for a completed action. Change ません to ませんでした for an action you did not do.
